owner.name: Spencer Brake
owner.tagline: Builder of practical apps for real, often overlooked places.
owner.blurb: I build useful systems for places where the usual assumptions do not hold.
owner.about: I am a builder and systems architect focused on the operational layer: how people move, pay, queue, book, dispatch, discover work, and keep track of what matters. I live and work in the remote North of Canada, where I work in retail management and build around the constraints I see firsthand—spotty connectivity, no card payments, civic-number addresses, field work, and people who should not need a manual. I am also a sound engineer and a certified minerals prospector, happiest panning for gold or looking at rocks. Through Presidia Corp, the problem-solving corporation, I turn real constraints into simple, durable tools that fit the place they are meant to serve.

projects.name: KnowYourLocal
projects.description: A peer-to-peer handyman marketplace where people can find local workers through availability and work photos, while tradespeople find jobs and get paid through Stripe Connect escrow only after the work is done.

projects.name: Chewdash Taxi
projects.tagline: Ride-booking for a remote Nunavik town
projects.description: A simple local dispatch system for Kuujjuarapik: book a taxi, arrange food pickup from nearby spots, or request a snack delivery. The goal is an interface anyone can use without instruction.

projects.name: Ponte
projects.description: A private video-call tool with live translated captions, built to make a long-distance conversation feel natural across a language barrier. Live and in daily use.

projects.name: Weedback
projects.description: A consumer-led cannabis grading system: ten user-scored metrics become an algorithmic score out of 100 and a grade from A- through AAAA+, organized by batch, strain, brand, and licensed producer.

projects.name: Northern Utility Dispatch
projects.tagline: Oil, water & sewage dispatch for the North
projects.description: A shared request-to-dispatch-to-driver workflow for oil, water, and sewage deliveries, giving residents, dispatchers, and drivers the same status and delivery details across northern Quebec and Nunavut.

projects.name: Q
projects.description: A geo-fenced queue for bars and clubs that lets people wait somewhere warm instead of standing outside in rain or snow, while venues move guests through faster and see live occupancy.

projects.name: SpennyBurger
projects.description: A direct ordering and payment portal built because Facebook messages were impossible to answer while cooking. Customers order and pay; the kitchen marks the order ready and the customer gets a pickup text.

projects.name: eProspector
projects.description: A shared exploration workspace for anyone interested in prospecting: pin a find, check claims, attach photos, and decide whether to keep it with the team or make it public.

projects.name: Invstar
projects.description: A department-manager inventory system for remote operations. Track units across warehouses, sea cans, freezers, coolers, dry storage, and backrooms; tap when a unit is used; and get reorder guidance based on stock, daily use, and lead time.

projects.name: MetalPRO Terminal
projects.description: A shared research terminal built with my dad for watching precious metals, mining equities, energy, rare earths, and strategic minerals in one place, with live prices, charts, futures curves, and keyboard-driven views.

projects.name: COMMAND NODE
projects.tagline: Real-time global warfare, Cold War console
projects.description: A real-time conquest game combining live fronts, long-term planning, persistent world state, and the atmosphere of a Cold War command room.
